purpose: Teach: キュウリ/とうもろこし/にっこり/ガソリンスタンド/ホームセンター/クラスメート/うっすら/気さく

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、ばあさんの、絶対、キュウリ、絶対、漬物、絶対、お父さん、絶対、大好きだったぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When I was young, I remember how much I absolutely loved your grandmother's pickled cucumbers. Do you remember that?
lines.style: Slow, distant gaze. Voice catches softly on the word 'loved'—not sad, but tender with the weight of decades. Warm exhale at the end, like settling into a chair.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。畑で、本気で、絶対、とうもろこし、絶対、お父さん、絶対、たくさん、絶対、育てたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: I do. I remember how we grew so much corn in the field back then. You remember, don't you, dear?
lines.style: Gentle, affirming nod in the voice. Each phrase lands with quiet presence. Slow tempo. A slight lift at 'dear'—the tenderness of long knowing someone.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 孫が、本気で、絶対、にっこり、絶対、お父さんに、絶対、笑ってくれたぞ、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: And the grandchildren would smile so brightly at your father. Do you remember that, grandmother?
lines.style: Voice softens to almost a whisper on 'smile.' Tender without sentimentality. Pause before 'grandmother'—a deliberate reaching toward her across time.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 昔、本気で、絶対、町に、絶対、ガソリンスタンド、絶対、できた時、絶対、賑わったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Back then, when the gas station came to town, everything became so lively. You remember how it was, don't you, dear?
lines.style: Eyes light subtly in the voice. Conversational warmth. Medium pace. She's pulling a specific memory forward, trusting he'll see it too.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、ホームセンター、絶対、なかったから、絶対、何でも、絶対、自作したぞ、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When I was young, we didn't have hardware stores, so we had to make everything ourselves. You remember that, grandmother?
lines.style: Matter-of-fact pride underneath. Steady, even cadence. A slight lift on 'ourselves'—the satisfaction of what they managed.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃の、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃんの、絶対、クラスメート、絶対、皆、絶対、お元気かしらね、あなた
lines.en: I wonder how your grandfather's classmates are doing now. Everyone from those days—are they all well, I wonder?
lines.style: Trailing, conversational thought. Voice drifts slightly upward at the end—genuine wondering, not expecting an answer. Gentle, unfocused gaze.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 朝、本気で、絶対、うっすら、絶対、霜が、絶対、降りていたぞ、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: In the mornings, there was always a light frost on the ground. Do you remember that, grandmother?
lines.style: Quiet, observational. Breath slightly visible in the words—cold air. Slow pace. The memory arrives before the words do.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、本気で、絶対、若い頃から、絶対、気さくな、絶対、性格だったわよ、あなた
lines.en: Your grandfather was always such a friendly, easygoing person, even when he was young. You remember that about him, don't you?
lines.style: Warm certainty. Voice steady, affirming. A slight emphasis on 'always'—the constancy of who he was. Close, intimate register.
